data.comparison: Round-5 close, merged across all four groups. Pool minimum condition is unchanged at [5,5,7,7] 0.794099 A, so the band ceiling stays 0.814099 A and every tested arm is eligible; total condition spread is ~0.002 A and the leader sits ~0.0184 A inside the ceiling, so condition is non-binding and the ranking is effectively functional gap. Merging the four group anchors changes the leader: [8,7,7,3] is 0.795746 A / 3.624688 pIC50, better than [7,7,5,1] 0.796448 / 3.625798, [7,7,5,2] 0.796241 / 3.625862 and far better than [9,7,7,3] 0.802333 / 3.651607. G1 and G2 could not see the sibling 8-arm and each named its own anchor leader; the merged band-then-gap leader is [8,7,7,3]. The largest new fact is the matched interval-0 7->8 edge: [8,7,7,3] versus executed [7,7,7,3] gives -0.000134 A and -0.001233 pIC50, the biggest single-interval functional gain measured since 5->7, while 9 is adverse on a second background. Interval-0 = 8 is therefore the operating value and G1:H2's forecast of a trailing 8-arm (made before the 8-arm read out) is superseded. Combined with the round-5 release measurements (3->1 -0.000118 pIC50, 3->2 -0.000054), the arms are ranked by their predicted terminal gap against 3.624688, not against their own action anchors: G1:H2 [8,7,5,1] ~3.62457, G3:H1 [8,7,7,1] ~3.62457 (the two are within 1e-5 pIC50 of each other and differ only in attribution cleanliness), G2:H2 [8,7,5,2] ~3.62463, G3:H2 [8,7,5,3] ~3.62468, then G1:H1 and its duplicate G2:H1 [7,7,5,0] ~3.62574, G4:H1 [7,7,7,1] ~3.62580 and G4:H2 [7,7,7,2] ~3.62587. Best is 7.2115-7.2157 against teacher 7.83783 and no arm exceeds the teacher, so the Best bonus never justifies an in-band mean loss. search_budget reports remaining_sampling_rounds 0 with decision_phase review_only, so all eight are archive-only suggestions and cannot displace the cached leader this session.
data.failure_directions: Interval-0 = 8 is measured only through the [7,7,7,3] contrast; the two leading arms carry it onto untested backgrounds (interval-2=5 in G1:H2 and G2:H2, interval-3=1 in G3:H1 and G1:H2). If those land at or above 3.624688 the 8 edge is background-specific and the ~3.62457 forecast for the top two arms, and the reason they outrank the cached leader, both fail. The interval-3 release may reverse at 1 (near-zero guidance is a regime boundary): a flat or adverse 3->1 would leave 3->2 as the floor and remove the predicted gain in G3:H1, G1:H2 and G4:H1. All four selected arms share interval 0 = 8 and the release direction, so one common failure takes the whole frontier; the only supplied interval-0 = 7 alternatives, G4:H1 [7,7,7,1] and G4:H2 [7,7,7,2], are forecast to trail the leader by roughly 0.0011 pIC50 and the supplied set therefore offers no strong hedge — that limitation is stated, not patched with invented arrays. G3:H2 is an attribution test rather than a forecast win: if interval-2 = 7 actually carries part of the leader's gap, removing it loses more than the 5e-6 predicted, and its near-tie status would be wrong. Finally, no result from this round can be observed, so no part of this ranking constitutes confirmation, and Best never exceeds the teacher so it cannot rescue a mean regression.

Teacher 5nn4_SC2_A_1017__top1, v26. Fixed new R0 before update 10 for every schedule, common 25-candidate stream, 25/25 valid throughout. Condition = protein-fixed terminal mean of per-candidate core-atom (7,9) RMSD; band = pool minimum + 0.02 A; function = mean absolute affinity gap to teacher 7.837829 pIC50 (lower better); Best is a bonus only and no arm exceeds the teacher.

BAND AND MERGED LEADER (round-5 close, 21 tested schedules): pool minimum unchanged at [5,5,7,7] 0.794099 A, so ceiling 0.814099 A and every arm is inside with ~0.002 A total condition spread. Merged band-then-gap leader is [8,7,7,3] 0.795746 A / 3.624688 pIC50 (margin ~0.0184 A), ahead of [7,7,5,1] 0.796448/3.625798, [7,7,5,2] 0.796241/3.625862, [7,7,5,3] 0.796032/3.625916, [7,7,7,3] 0.795880/3.625921, [7,9,5,3] 0.795957/3.625982, [7,7,7,5] 0.795462/3.626059, [7,5,5,3] 0.795696/3.626080. Condition is non-binding, so challengers must be argued as gap reductions below 3.624688.

ROUND-5 EDGES: interval 0 7->8 on [7,7,7,3] gives -0.000134 A / -0.001233 pIC50, the largest single-interval functional gain since 5->7, so 8 is the operating value, not 7. Interval 0 = 9 is adverse on a second background ([9,7,7,3] 0.802333/3.651607 vs [9,7,5,3] 0.802451/3.651566), so 9 is rejected. Interval 3 3->1 gives +0.0004155 A / -0.000118 pIC50 and 3->2 gives +0.000209 A / -0.000054, continuing release below the old floor of 3 at ~2e-4 A/tick and ~5-6e-5 pIC50/tick; 0 is the only untested remainder and is a regime boundary. Interval 2 5->7 stays a condition-only micro-lever (-0.000152 A / +0.000005 on [7,7,7,3]; -0.000118 A / +0.000041 on the 9 background). Interval 1 held at 7 (7->9 +0.000066; 5->7 attenuates -0.000275 then -0.000164; 7->5 costs +0.000164).

MEDIATOR unchanged: clip_factor 1.0 and clipped fraction 0.0 everywhere; delivered max-atom guidance ~1e-3 A against a 0.35-1.42 A per-candidate spread, so delivery is not the bottleneck and the open question is which interval's displacement survives the unguided 91-99 tail. Candidate-intrinsic residual dominates; only 5/25 candidates map to a legal teacher subgraph (pose RMSD mean 0.954 A), so coordinates do not directly constrain chemistry or affinity.

DEDUPLICATION: G1:H1 and G2:H1 are both [7,7,5,0]; duplicate execution is not independent evidence. No supplied arm replicates the leader [8,7,7,3].

BUDGET: remaining_sampling_rounds 0, decision_phase review_only; all eight proposals are archive-only and cannot displace the cached leader.

FALSIFIER: any arm moving group mean condition by >=0.005 A or |delta gap| >=0.001 pIC50 versus its reference breaks the weak-lever belief. Specific: release below 3 is closed at 1 if [8,7,7,1] does not fall below 3.624688; the interval-0 8 edge is background-specific if the 8-arms at interval-2=5 or interval-3=1/2 trail the leader.

learning_update.revision: Interval-1 low is expected to be a weak falsifier at best; it is not an expected leader challenger, but it tests whether the new leader background changes the local interval-1 response.
learning_update.next_action: Archive only; a flat or worse result closes this local interval-1 low branch.
learning_update.applicability: Interval 1 on teacher v26 and the measured fixed-population background; not proof of universal interval-1 inertness.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: A small interaction with interval 2 = 3 or interval 0 = 1 could make interval-1 low active on this background even though it was near-null elsewhere.

data.parent_policy: Every proposal restarts the same new R0 before update 10. Incumbent is output only.

action_contract.double_tick_rule: Two ticks allowed by default; three only in verified_large_step_directions.
action_contract.range_probe_rule: Only after range expansion; at most one of final four. Max two changed intervals. Fine grid remains 0.1. Explain actual jump vs coarse default; all other proposals are local.
action_contract.reference_semantics: Action deltas use this current group anchor. Fixed R0 before update 10 is the physical restart only. Historical causal comparisons do not replace the action anchor.
